subsystems.name: Inner rotor
subsystems.role: a continuous loop of cable or magnetically levitated mass moving faster than local orbital velocity; its excess centrifugal force is what holds the whole structure up.
parts: high-strength cable or segmented mass stream

subsystems.name: Outer sheath
subsystems.role: the non-orbiting platform that the rotor pushes against, giving a stationary ring to build on.

subsystems.name: Deck and habitats
subsystems.role: the usable surface: transit lines, solar arrays, docks, pressurised habitat modules.

subsystems.name: Power and drive
subsystems.role: keeps the rotor moving against drag and levitation losses, and spins it up from rest.

subsystems.name: Ground connections
subsystems.role: tethers, cables or elevator shafts linking the stationary ring to the planet at fixed points.

subsystems.name: Self-replicating factory
subsystems.role: the conceptual 'self-assembling' part — machines that mine, refine and copy themselves to build the ring without launching everything from the ground.

buildSteps.title: Bootstrap off-planet industry
buildSteps.detail: Begin with a small mining and refining outpost on a low-gravity body — the Moon or a near-Earth asteroid — where material can be launched cheaply with electromagnetic mass drivers rather than rockets.

buildSteps.title: Seed a self-replicating factory
buildSteps.detail: Land a small set of machines that can build copies of themselves from local rock and metal. Each generation doubles the industrial capacity; this is the key assumption the whole plan rests on.

buildSteps.title: Mass-produce structural cable
buildSteps.detail: The factory spins cable or pultrudes segmented beams in vacuum, where oxidation and handling limits that constrain such materials on Earth are relaxed. Tens of thousands of kilometres are needed for a ring around Earth.

buildSteps.title: Launch the components
buildSteps.detail: Completed sections are flung into orbit by the same electromagnetic launchers, meeting the ring plane at a chosen altitude above the atmosphere.

buildSteps.title: Close the rotor loop
buildSteps.detail: Segments are captured, joined and gently nudged into a single closed loop travelling just above local orbital speed — about 7.8 km/s in low Earth orbit.

buildSteps.title: Spin the rotor up
buildSteps.detail: Linear accelerators push the loop faster, so its outward force exceeds the pull of gravity. The magnets now carry the loop rather than letting it orbit freely.

buildSteps.title: Wrap the sheath around it
buildSteps.detail: Containment tube and structural spine are threaded onto the moving loop and magnetically coupled to it, so the stationary outer ring is held aloft.

buildSteps.title: Anchor and load the deck
buildSteps.detail: Tethers to the surface are installed at a few points to stop the ring drifting, then transit lines, solar arrays and habitats are added.

buildSteps.title: Operate and expand
buildSteps.detail: The ring is kept spinning against drag and losses, and used as a platform and as a launch track for payloads going further out.

prerequisites.why: no machine today can mine, refine and manufacture a full copy of itself; the ring's economics depend entirely on this.
the rotor must survive tension over enormous lengths with minimal mass; the best candidates have never been made in bulk kilometres.

prerequisites.tech: Maglev and linear accelerators at megawatt–gigawatt scale
prerequisites.why: demonstrated for trains and small launchers, but not for a multi-thousand-kilometre loop continuously.

prerequisites.tech: Non-rocket launch from a low-gravity body
prerequisites.why: electromagnetic launchers have been built for payloads, but not for the volumes of material a ring needs.
only small experiments so far; the ring assumes an entire off-Earth supply chain.

pathway.milestone: reusable rockets cutting launch cost, and early in-orbit manufacturing experiments
pathway.unlocks: routine access to orbit and the first off-Earth products.

pathway.milestone: a working orbital ring around a small low-gravity body, built by self-replicating machines
pathway.unlocks: proof that the concept is buildable at all, and cheap material in space.

pathway.milestone: planetary-scale ring segments and ground tethers
pathway.unlocks: a stationary platform above a planet and a launch track that reaches orbit without fuel.

pathway.milestone: a full ring around Earth or another planet
pathway.unlocks: very low-cost surface-to-orbit transport and large habitable area in orbit — the classic alternative to a space elevator.
